title: University Security & Privacy Assessment Questionnaire
description: Assessment questionnaire for evaluating cybersecurity, privacy, and regulatory compliance of Indian universities.

questions.question: Does your institution publish a privacy notice that clearly explains how personal data is collected, used, stored, shared, and protected?
Before collecting personal data, does your institution obtain valid consent or rely on another documented lawful basis for processing where applicable?
Does your institution maintain an up-to-date inventory of personal and institutional data, including where it is stored and processed?
Is institutional data classified according to its sensitivity (for example, public, internal, confidential, or restricted) and handled accordingly?
Does your institution define and follow documented retention periods for different categories of personal and institutional data?
When data is no longer required, does your institution securely delete, destroy, or anonymize it using documented procedures?
Does your institution collect only the minimum amount of personal data necessary to achieve a specific and legitimate purpose?
Is every category of personal data collected and processed only for clearly defined, documented, and legitimate institutional purposes?
Does your institution have documented procedures to receive, verify, process, and respond to requests from individuals regarding their personal data?
Are sensitive categories of personal data protected using additional technical and organizational safeguards beyond standard security measures?
Are users granted access only to the systems, applications, and information necessary to perform their assigned responsibilities, following the principle of least privilege?
Are user roles and permissions formally defined so that access rights are assigned based on job responsibilities rather than individual requests?
Is an additional authentication factor required for privileged, administrative, or remote access to institutional systems and applications?
Does your institution enforce password requirements such as minimum length, complexity, password history, secure storage, and protection against default or weak passwords?
Are privileged or administrator accounts separately managed, monitored, and restricted to authorized personnel with additional oversight?
Are user accounts promptly created, modified, reviewed, disabled, or removed in response to events such as onboarding, role changes, transfers, or employee separation?

Has your institution established, approved, communicated, and periodically reviewed an information security policy that defines security objectives, responsibilities, and acceptable use of institutional resources?
Does your institution maintain a complete inventory of hardware, software, databases, cloud services, and other information assets, including ownership and accountability?
Is sensitive institutional and personal data protected using appropriate encryption or equivalent safeguards when stored on servers, databases, backup media, laptops, or portable devices?
Is sensitive information protected during transmission between users, applications, systems, or external parties using secure communication protocols and encryption mechanisms?
Are operating systems, applications, databases, and network devices configured according to documented security baselines and periodically reviewed to prevent insecure configurations?
Does your institution have a documented process to identify, test, approve, and deploy security patches and updates within defined timelines based on their criticality?
Are regular vulnerability assessments, security scans, or penetration testing activities conducted to identify and remediate security weaknesses in institutional systems?
Are institution-owned systems protected by centrally managed anti-malware or endpoint protection solutions that are regularly updated and monitored?
Are desktops, laptops, workstations, and other endpoint devices secured through centralized policies, security monitoring, and device protection controls?

Are institution-owned or authorized mobile devices protected through security measures such as device encryption, screen locks, remote wipe capabilities, and mobile device management where appropriate?
Are institutional networks designed, configured, and maintained with appropriate security controls to protect systems, users, and sensitive information from unauthorized access and cyber threats?
Are firewalls configured according to documented security policies, regularly reviewed, and monitored to restrict unauthorized inbound and outbound network traffic?
Are critical systems, administrative networks, and sensitive institutional data isolated from general-purpose networks using logical or physical segmentation where appropriate?
Are remote connections to institutional systems protected using secure authentication methods, encrypted communication channels, and controlled access mechanisms?
If your institution uses cloud services, are cloud-hosted systems and data configured, monitored, and managed in accordance with documented security requirements and best practices?
Are servers hosting institutional applications, databases, or other critical services securely configured, regularly updated, continuously monitored, and protected against unauthorized access?

Are security-related activities, including user logins, privileged operations, system configuration changes, and access to sensitive information, recorded through audit logs that are protected from unauthorized modification and retained for investigation purposes?

Does your institution continuously monitor networks, systems, applications, and security events to detect suspicious activities, policy violations, or potential cybersecurity threats in a timely manner?
Does your institution maintain a documented incident response plan that clearly defines roles, responsibilities, communication procedures, containment, recovery, and post-incident review activities?
Are faculty, staff, and other authorized users provided with documented procedures to identify, report, and escalate suspected cybersecurity or privacy incidents through approved reporting channels?
Does your institution have documented procedures to assess, document, and notify the appropriate authorities or affected individuals when a reportable data breach or security incident occurs?
Are backups of critical systems, applications, databases, and institutional data created regularly, securely protected, periodically tested, and capable of being successfully restored when required?
Has your institution established, documented, and periodically tested disaster recovery procedures to restore critical IT services within defined recovery objectives following major disruptions?

Does your institution maintain and periodically test a business continuity plan to ensure that essential academic, administrative, and operational activities can continue during significant disruptions or emergencies?
Does your institution perform documented cybersecurity and privacy risk assessments at planned intervals and whenever significant organizational, technological, or regulatory changes occur?

Before engaging third-party vendors or service providers that access, process, or store institutional or personal data, does your institution evaluate their security, privacy, and compliance capabilities?
Does your institution periodically reassess third-party vendors throughout the duration of their engagement to ensure continued compliance with contractual security and privacy requirements?

Are students, faculty, staff, and other authorized users provided with regular cybersecurity and privacy awareness training appropriate to their roles, responsibilities, and emerging security threats?
Does your institution follow a documented change management process that evaluates, approves, tests, documents, and reviews significant changes before they are deployed into production environments?

Are internal security and compliance audits conducted periodically to verify adherence to institutional policies, regulatory obligations, and security controls, with identified findings tracked until remediation is complete?

Are student records, examination data, academic information, and other student-related personal data protected throughout their lifecycle using appropriate technical, administrative, and organizational security measures?
Are personal records of faculty and staff securely collected, processed, stored, accessed, retained, and disposed of in accordance with institutional policies and applicable legal requirements?

If your institution conducts research involving digital research data or personal information, are appropriate security, privacy, access control, and backup measures implemented to protect research assets throughout their lifecycle?

Are the institution's Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP), Learning Management System (LMS), Student Information System (SIS), and other academic platforms securely configured, regularly updated, protected by appropriate access controls, and continuously monitored against security threats?
